subject: physics
question_text: A vehicle travels half the distance L with speed V₁ and the other half with speed V₂. What is its average velocity?

verification.note: Unit 3 has NO Long Answer section in either source book. The Fastrack (pp.6-8) lists 4 Very Short Answer and 6 Short Answer questions; the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.4-5) has a Short Answer section ONLY and no VSAQ section at all. So this VSAQ is the Fastrack’s alone. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: The two times
lines: Each half covers a distance L/2, so
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
steps.why: The two halves take different times, so the slower half occupies more of the journey. That is why the two speeds cannot simply be averaged.
common_mistakes: Assuming each half takes the same time, which leads to the wrong answer (V₁+V₂)/2.

recall.must_convey: That each half is L over two, so the times are L over two V one and L over two V two.

steps.memory_tip: Equal DISTANCES, not equal times. The slower half takes more time.
steps.margin_note: Write both times before combining them.

steps.label: The average
steps.why: This is the harmonic mean of the two speeds, and it always comes out smaller than the ordinary average, because more time is spent at the slower speed.
common_mistakes: Writing (V₁+V₂)/2, which would be right only if the two halves took equal TIMES.

recall.must_convey: That the average velocity is two V one V two divided by V one plus V two.
accept: two V one V two by V one plus V two
reject: V one plus V two by two

steps.memory_tip: Equal distances give 2V₁V₂/(V₁+V₂). Equal times would give (V₁+V₂)/2.

insider_note: A 3-star cell. The answer is the harmonic mean, not (V₁+V₂)/2 — equal DISTANCES, not equal times.
